params.body:
In a conversation the model knew the full site list and his four recent sites, and nothing about what happens on a site. Bouwsoft does know that: per project, which machines and materials were booked and who worked there. So a worker who said "Stabil" and then "de kraan" got a generic question, and a colleague's or material's name had nothing to be recognised against. On screen, sites showed as tap buttons only until one site was on the sheet, machines always, and materials never.

## The conversation gets the options of a site

`SiteOptions` reads `reference_bookings` for a site over the last 42 days. It gives:
- the machines (8), materials (8) and colleagues (6, not himself), most days first;
- only names the catalogue or the staff list knows.

They reach the model at three moments, each site once:

- **In the prompt**, under each of his recent sites (`hisSites`).
- **On a tap** of a site, in the message that tells the model about the tap.
- **When he names a site.** The answer to the write that put it on the sheet carries a `context` field. The browser adds it to the conversation as a system item, without `response.create`, so nothing is said until he speaks again. The tool call itself is still answered at once, as before.

Which sites were told is cached per worksheet for four hours, and reset when a new conversation starts.

The prompt keeps the rule it has for suggested sites and machines: the options help to ask a precise question ("de rupskraan of de minikraan?") and to recognise a name. The model never puts one on the sheet because it is listed, and never asks about something only because it is listed.

## Options to tap, in the flow of the conversation

- **Step panel.** While the model asks about the site, the machines or the material (the card already lights up), that step's options stand in a panel right above the microphone:
  - for the site: his recent sites not on the sheet yet, which also works for a second site on the same day;
  - for machines: the existing machine suggestions;
  - for material: the materials of the site.
  The board hides its own copy of that step meanwhile. The invitation on an empty day keeps its site buttons.
- **Materials can be tapped.** A material booked on the site appears on the board after the material cards, and also in the step panel. A tap puts it on the sheet with its unit and tells the model to take it over by its exact name and ask how much.
  - Only articles whose name the catalogue knows for exactly one article are offered, so the name the model hands back finds the same row.
  - `article_lines.chosen_at` (new) keeps a tapped material through a reading made before the model knew about it, the same as for sites and machines.

## Tests

- `SiteOptionsTest`:
  - options per site, most days first, without himself, with ambiguous names left out of the tap list;
  - the prompt carries them under his recent sites;
  - a tapped site brings them in its message;
  - a spoken site brings them once in the write answer, and not again;
  - a tapped material lands, survives an earlier reading and takes the quantity after;
  - the step panel offers his other sites.
- JS: a `context` in the write answer reaches the model as a system item without a turn.
- Full suite 245/245, JS 14/14, pint clean.
- Checked on a copy of the production-size database at phone width: the material step panel above the microphone, with the Materiaal card lit up.

After merge: `php artisan migrate` (one column).
